note: A Rust panic (or body-stream error) after the response header in a header-first streaming dispatch no longer depends on the servlet container's error page. The JNI streaming symbols throw com.devfive.vespera.bridge.VesperaStreamAbortedException (an IOException; panicked() flags a Rust panic, falling back to a plain IOException with the same message when the class cannot be resolved), and the Spring proxy (BIDIRECTIONAL_STREAMING, STREAMING and the stashed DIRECT overflow stream) answers it with its own 500 ('panic in Rust engine', DispatchEvent.panicked / outcome=PANIC) while the response is uncommitted, dropping the Rust 200 status, headers and partial body; once bytes reached the client the connection is still aborted, so a truncated response never ends cleanly. Regression tests cover the inline small-body and producer request paths.
